title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Case Binder. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Case Binder
options.thesis: Projects open as evidence tabs; specialty is the spine; contact sits on the open sheet.
options.viewport: Open binder on a desk: live Project 01 tab, large plate, contact links on the sheet edge.
options.risk: Reads corporate HR kit if tabs get timid — keep spine red and proof oversized.

raised.raise: Skills and projects read as a connected force network — linked members, not isolated chips.
One oversized specialty word on the sheet; nav as thin tracked labels at the margins.
Projects stay an unbroken addressable sequence — tabs never wrap into a card grid.
One tab/lobe owns each viewport; the next section starts only after a full coast change.

options.label: Presentation Board
options.thesis: A single presentation board: title block, one dominant project plate, contact in the footer strip.
options.viewport: Full-bleed board with name as title block and one oversized project plate as proof.
options.risk: Also the direction most specialty portfolios land on — familiar, effective.

options.label: Spy Dossier
options.thesis: Hiring as case-file review: project frames under a reticle, name typed in, contact as the red stamp.
options.viewport: Manila field with typed name, three project frames, reticle on the lead, CONTACT stamp.
options.case: Beats the binder on hiring-manager identification and contact clarity — evaluation as file review.
options.risk: Camp spy pastiche if the stamp and reticle play as jokes instead of evidence tools.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: The portfolio as a building section: project rooms gather along the moving edge of useful light.
options.viewport: Long section cut: dark poche left, sunbeam across one occupied project room.
options.case: Holds craft-evaluation identification; slower contact path than stamp or sheet links.
options.risk: Architecture costume if solar poetry outranks project proof.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.case: Hiring managers do not identify with structural sculpture; contact path dissolves into force diagrams.
options.kept: Connected tension network — donated as linked skills/projects.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.case: Shader spectacle buries specialty and contact; fails hiring clarity.
options.kept: Oversized specialty word + thin margin labels — donated as sheet hierarchy.

options.label: Step Row
options.case: Music-gear identification misses hiring managers; projects-as-beats muddies proof.
options.kept: Unbroken addressable sequence — donated as non-wrapping project tabs.

options.label: Guide Map
options.case: Leisure-map culture fights hiring seriousness; cream-and-green defaults the category soft look.
options.kept: One lobe owns the viewport — donated as single-tab ownership.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark hero, role headline, skill pills, project cards — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name and specialty over a portrait and a Get in touch button; skills as pills.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from competing engineer portfolios by design.
